body_markdown:
Across government and higher education, AI is becoming part of daily activities, helping people find and summarize information faster, automate routine tasks, analyze information and spend more time on higher-value priorities. In April 2026, the U.S. Government Accountability Office reported that federal agencies had more than doubled their use of AI from 2023 to 2024 and continued acquiring additional AI capabilities through fiscal year 2025.¹


AI is also becoming part of team meetings. AI-powered capabilities can capture notes and action items, summarize conversations, translate captions and help participants catch up on discussions they missed. As these capabilities become more common, expectations for the technology and spaces around people are changing too.


Research conducted by Market Connections and sponsored by Logitech found that 62% of federal technology leaders say shared workspaces are not adequately equipped for hybrid collaboration. Half report frequent IT support needs simply to start or join meetings, while 40% say remote attendees struggle to be fully included.²


As AI becomes embedded in everyday workflows, people will increasingly expect the capabilities to carry with them into meeting rooms, classrooms and shared spaces.


**For IT leaders, that raises a practical question: Are personal and team workspaces ready to keep pace with the capabilities organizations are putting in place?**


## Start with the Individual Workspace


For many people, the individual workspace is where new AI and productivity capabilities become part of their day. It is where they find information, create and analyze content, communicate and collaborate.


The experience still depends on the technology people use to interact with it. Webcams and headsets help people communicate clearly and participate fully, while keyboards and mice can make navigating digital workflows more comfortable and efficient.


One configuration, however, will not fit every role. An analyst working primarily from an office may have different needs than a faculty member, administrator or someone moving between locations.


Logitech Personal Workspace solutions help IT standardize around those different roles and needs, creating a more consistent experience while simplifying deployment and support.


[Tailored Workspaces](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/business/resource-center/e-books/employee-workspace-solutions.html?utm_campaign=nam_google-public-sector-summit&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=article&utm_content=pws_employee_types_and_work_desks_ebook&utm_term=fy27q2) provides a framework for matching workspace solutions to how and where people use technology.


These investments matter. Logitech’s federal research found that 57% of respondents identify personal collaboration devices as essential investments for workforce effectiveness.²


**The opportunity is to give people the right tools to get more from evolving technology while giving IT a more consistent, manageable environment.**


## Bring the Experience Into Shared Spaces


The need to connect and collaborate extends beyond the individual workspace. Across government and higher education, people move into meeting rooms, classrooms and shared spaces to exchange information, bring together expertise, teach, learn and make decisions.


In these spaces, the experience still depends on being able to connect easily, see and hear one another clearly, share information and fully include people joining from other locations.


Logitech


[Team Workspace solutions](https://www.logitech.com/content/dam/logitech/en/video-collaboration/pdf/workspace-guide-for-google-meet.pdf) help create a more consistent experience across these environments. Clear audio and video also provide better inputs for AI-powered capabilities such as transcription, meeting summaries and other intelligent meeting features. Logitech solutions can also help organizations rethink open or underused areas as flexible spaces for people to gather and collaborate.


**The result is more places where people can connect with information, expertise and one another.**


## Standardize User Experiences, Simplify Management


More intelligent technology should not mean greater complexity for users or IT.


In Logitech’s federal research, 31% of respondents said varying technology configurations across rooms or buildings challenge ad hoc collaboration.²


Standardization can help reduce that complexity. Personal workspace standards can simplify endpoint deployment and support. Consistent room configurations can make collaboration experiences more predictable across buildings and locations. Logitech Sync can give IT teams visibility into compatible devices and help them remotely monitor and manage collaboration technology.


Government and higher education organizations may also need to account for procurement, security, accessibility and compliance requirements when establishing technology standards. For government organizations with applicable procurement requirements,


[TAA-compliant options](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/business/resource-center/article/taa-ndaa-compliant-products.html??utm_campaign=nam_google-public-sector-summit&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=article&utm_content=taa_compliant_solutions_article&utm_term=fy27q2) across the Logitech portfolio can support broader standardization strategies.


**Effective standardization creates environments that are intuitive for people to use and easier for IT to deploy, support and manage at scale.**


## Extend the Experience Beyond Traditional Spaces


Government services, education and research extend beyond traditional offices and classrooms. Field teams, inspectors, public safety personnel, educators and other mobile users may need to access information, communicate and collaborate across locations.


Mobile devices extend that experience across locations. Logitech mobility solutions can help equip users with tools for typing, navigation, protection and interaction across different devices and environments.


For IT, mobility is another consideration in supporting people across locations and use cases.


## What to Watch Next


AI is moving quickly. The bigger story to watch is how it changes the way people serve, teach, learn, collaborate and get things done, and what that means for the technology and spaces around them.


For IT leaders, the opportunity is to build environments that can evolve with those changing expectations. That means considering the entire experience, from individual workspaces to shared environments, while balancing usability, manageability, compliance and long-term investment.


The


[Google Public Sector Summit](https://events.govexec.com/google-public-sector-summit/) offers one opportunity to see that strategy in action. Attendees can experience Logitech solutions for Google Meet firsthand, including TAA-compliant options for government, and discuss how existing environments can evolve through a proof of concept.


That strategy can extend beyond any single platform or event. Organizations can start with the spaces and users that matter most, evaluate what works and build a technology foundation that can adapt as needs and capabilities change.


**AI is changing how people get things done. The technology and spaces around them will evolve too. That’s the transformation worth watching.**
